seoTitle: How to Color Code Asana Tasks for Faster Scanning
metaDescription: Learn how to color code tasks, tags, and custom fields in Asana in 2026 so you can prioritize deadlines and scan project boards at a glance.
intro: A cluttered project board slows everyone down, and color coding in Asana is one of the simplest ways to make priorities and categories instantly visible. This guide covers assigning colors to tags, building color-coded custom fields for priority levels, and keeping your workspace visually consistent across projects.

steps.heading: Open a task and access tag colors
steps.body: Select a task card, open the tag dropdown panel, and assign or customize the color tied to each tag.

steps.heading: Build color-coded custom fields
steps.body: Use the project customization menu to create a custom field, such as Priority, with distinct colors for values like High, Medium, and Low.

steps.heading: Apply colors across phases or assignees
steps.body: Use color accents to visually separate project phases, departments, or assignees so you can skim the board without reading every label.

steps.heading: Set up automated color rules
steps.body: Configure workspace automation rules so task colors change automatically based on status updates or other triggers.

steps.heading: Keep the scheme consistent
steps.body: Standardize your color choices across projects so the same color always means the same thing, avoiding visual overload.

faq.question: Can I color code individual tasks, not just tags?
faq.answer: Task headers can take on color through tags and custom fields, since Asana ties visual color to these categorization tools rather than the task title itself.

faq.question: Will color-coded custom fields sync across board and list views?
faq.answer: Yes, custom field colors display consistently whether you're viewing the project as a board, list, or timeline.

faq.question: Can automation rules change colors automatically?
faq.answer: Yes, you can set up rules so a task's color-coded field updates automatically when its status changes.

faq.question: Is there a limit to how many colors I can use?
faq.answer: Asana offers a fixed palette for tags and custom fields, so plan your color scheme around that set rather than unlimited custom hues.
